title: Migration Merkle leaf omits reciever, so any holder of the public L1 signature can redirect another contract's migration credit to an attacker-chosen L2 address
description: verifyDepositsAndInternalBalances() computes the Merkle leaf as keccak256(abi.encode(account, deposits, internalBalances, ownerRoots)) — it commits to the L1 owner and the asset data but NOT to reciever. reciever (the L2 destination of the credit) is bound only by the separate EIP-712 signature in verifySignature() over (owner, reciever, deadline). The signature is presented in the public L2 transaction calldata. Combined with CC-001's lack of replay protection, the (owner, reciever, deadline) tuple and signature are observable on-chain, and because the Merkle proof does not constrain reciever, the redeem function will accept any reciever for which a matching signature is presented. There is no on-chain link forcing reciever to equal the original migrant, so credit can be steered to an attacker address as part of a replay.
impact: The migration deposit/stalk/roots credit for an L1 contract can be redirected to and/or duplicated at an attacker-chosen L2 address using the publicly visible signature, rather than only the originally intended reciever. Standalone this is an authorization-binding gap; combined with CC-001 it converts replay into attacker-controlled theft of migrated value. High (Critical when chained with CC-001).

ite.intent: Bind migration credit immutably to the intended L2 reciever
ite.technique: reciever excluded from the Merkle leaf; only a replayable signature binds it
ite.evasion: Use the on-chain-visible signature; the proof check imposes no constraint on reciever

ice_chain.corrupted_state: s.accts[reciever].deposits / .stalk / .roots credited to an address not committed by the proof
ice_chain.consumer_function: silo deposit, stalk and roots consumers (withdraw, earned-Bean distribution, governance)
ice_chain.impact: Migration credit redirection / duplication to attacker-controlled reciever
ice_chain.exploit_path: obtain the public owner signature -> call redeem with an unbound reciever -> proof passes (reciever absent from leaf) -> credit lands at chosen reciever
